I probably should have ordered it but I got confused there were so many choices and I wanted to try the Thai food for sure. Maybe Vietnamese next time they even have pho soups! I ordered a bowl of tom ga and it was excellent. Loaded with nice fresh mushrooms big pieces of fish scallions just enough pepper and a nice creamy broth. I ordered a Thai style pork with Thai broccoli and the pork turned out to be something like back bacon and not your usual slices of mystery meat. A nice fatty crust and two layers of fleshy meat cut in cubes so it looks like a layer cake each piece. Actually not too bad at all. Should have ordered it slightly spicier I asked for medium and it was well below the spice threshold for heat. I don't know why they call it broccoli it's more like nice slices of stem cooked just right and leafy parts that more resembled bok choy or spinach. A nice bowl of done properly rice, how many people do Rice properly these days? Ordered a Thai iced tea and even that was correct which is really surprising in Columbus. Only Thai Town in LA or the Thai Beach at Topanga and the Malibu border on Pacific Coast Highway matched this. You get spoiled in places like Los Angeles or New York or overseas where they do food right. This place is worth the drive down to that part of town. When I go back I'm doing the Vietnamese thing.

It also came with freshly chopped cucumber, which was unexpected and a good compliment to the chicken. This all by itself would make for a good light lunch or is plenty for 2 - 4 people to share.

The curry portion was huge. One entree could easily be split by two people, especially when you share an appetizer.

I like that they have an easy way to address how spicy you want things: timid, careful, adventurous and native lao. I went with the "careful" level of spiciness. The level of heat did not overwhelm the complex flavors for me, but next time I'll go for "timid" since it did start to get intense toward the end.

The leftovers re-heated well, but I think it was spicier than the meal was initially. Something to keep in mind if you're sensitive to spice and expect to bring some home for later.

So, I used to hate sushi.  My friends said that it was an acquired taste, that I would get used to the dead fish taste like I got used to beer.  One of the reasons it is, in fact, hard to get an opinion on sushi is that many people have acquired a taste for bad sushi, marked by the fact that it tastes like dead fish.  The Sapporo Wind, the ancestor of The Sapporo Sushi Factory, broke me of my hatred.  Turns out, good sushi doesn't taste like dead fish at all.

So, as I understand it, the owner of the Wind is the owner of the Factory and he is considered one of the best sushi chefs in the world.  The open-faced sushi, by the way, should not be feared.  It is called the Horo Special and it is delicious.  The sushi chef at the Factory is experimental, and that is what sets him above and apart from others. Even his experiments taste like good, traditional sushi at their base.

Having been to at least a dozen different chains including Mr. Sushi and Otani, I have to say that none of them give me that good food hum like the Factory.  Customers are treated well and I like the simplicity and the comfort of the decor.

When we walked in, we were greeted by a friendly hostess who also happened to be our server.  She allowed us to sit wherever we like.  We chose a booth near the entrance.  The first thing I noticed as I sat was that the seat had lost some of its cushion (I could feel the wood frame through it) - I am guessing the furniture is just old.  I also noticed that the carpet all around the restaurant was very old and in bad shape, showing the traffic lanes between tables; it really needs to be replaced.

She promptly asked us for our drink orders.  I got the Vietnamese iced coffee, and this was immediately a hit with me... perfectly sweet, perfectly strong, and served in a nice, big glass.

We both got sushi rolls and I also ordered some of the crab fried rice.  The sushi was very good, and it came out super quickly.  My roll was called the Rock & Roll, which was tempura battered and fried before being cut and served... it might be one of my favorite rolls ever, really impressive.

My fried rice came out before I was even finished with my sushi... the kitchen was on it!  I consider myself a fried rice connoisseur, so I was prepared to really judge them on it (much like how fries can be a good barometer for an American restaurant, it is my opinion that fried rice can be that for east Asian restaurants).  I finished my sushi before digging into the rice.  From the first bite, I was really pleased with the flavor!  The jasmine rice was still fragrant and very comforting.  However, there were a couple things I did notice about it that could be better.  This particular dish included pineapple, but I am fairly certain they used canned pineapples and didn't cook them at all; it would have been much better to grill fresh pineapple and toss that in.  Also, the menu specified the dish was made with lump crab meat, but this was not the case... they used imitation crab (could tell by how it had the shredded texture).  Now, to be fair, I did really enjoy the fried rice and I finished the whole thing - I even enjoy imitation crab; but if the menu specified lump crab meat, it should have been real crab.

So, we left full and happy.  The sushi especially was really impressive and reasonably priced.  There are some needed improvements as I suggested above... they really should update the furniture and flooring, and take to heart my feedback on the fried rice.  But don't mistake my constructive criticism for bashing - it was an all-around good experience and we will be back!

We've been to Big Bowl several times, most recently today for lunch. We waited a few minutes for a table which was expected because they were fairly busy. We were seated at a table by the window and it was a nice sunny day for February.

I started with a bowl of Hot and Sour soup. Big Bowl has the most delicious hot and sour soup I've had anywhere. I've had it at many restaurants.

For my entree I had the stir fry bar. Now they have a large menu so they have lots of great looking entrees to choose from, but for me the stir fry is the way I like to go. You get to go up and pick out your exact vegetables yourself. You get a clean bowl, and a clean pair of tongs and you go along and put your vegetables you want into your bowl. They have tons of choices to choose from including bok choy, bean sprouts, water chestnuts, baby corn, regular corn, peas, edamame, onions, white mushrooms, 2 other kinds of Asian mushrooms, broccoli, snow peas, bamboo shoots, green peppers, zucchini, jalapeno peppers, Anaheim peppers and habanero peppers. I've probably forgotten a few items but those are most of the choices. For the stir fry you also pick your protein (or no protein), choice of different noodles or rices, and choice of sauce. It's a really great setup you get to pick every component. It is always delicious. Today I picked my vegetables, no protein, Kung Pao sauce with peanuts and Chow Fun noodles (thick Asian noodles).

My wife had the Ahi Tuna Poke Bowl and really enjoyed the freshness of it.

My only complaint would be that our entrees were brought to the table after I had only had my soup for about 2 minutes. So I had to decide whether to let my soup get  cold and eat my entree or to finish my soup and let my entree get cold. I chose to eat my entree and let my soup get cold.

We highly recommend Big Bowl and hope you give it a try.

Summary: with some focus on service and attention to detail, this restaurant could be great.

Making your food look fancy and serving alcohol with the option of BYOB just doesn't cut it.  For those with the need for a gimmicky place to eat, here you go.

Free meal, but at what cost? EatStreet causes a major headache.

We ordered online—I think that was our first mistake. I would say ordering from No Thai! was our first mistake, but they did what they could to make it right.

The order went through a third party called GoMobo/OLO which has an odd system of putting a limited number of people into 15-minute blocks. We were placed into a later block automatically, so we knew ahead of time that we would be waiting an hour. But then they were 45 minutes late on top of that.

After a couple calls to No Thai!, the staff told us they didn't know where the driver was, and finally gave us the number for another company, EatStreet. My call was routed through a computer system, and I was put on hold for several minutes. Finally, I got someone who told me the driver was almost there. And there he was! Unfortunately the food was somewhat cold by that point.

Like I said, No Thai! tried to make it right, and gave us our order for free (at first it was 50% off, but then we had to wait another 20 minutes).

They are really doing themselves a disservice by contracting delivery through two other companies, GoMobo/OLO and EatStreet. It seems to cause more problems. I could have walked there rather than wait 1 hour and 45 minutes!

However I had asked for "hot" expecting typical thai flavorful spice. I can take the heat. I love it. But this was some of the most inconsistent heat I've ever had. In some spoonfuls it was crazy hot. Couldn't taste the potatoes or onions or tofu. At all. Just hot. In others it was like nothing was there. Just a weird dish overall. Was not impressed. Will be going to angels thai in the future.

Edited to add: 6 hours after I ate I've had the worse stomach cramps and pains I've had since I had appendicitis. My room mate also got an upset stomach after eating her noodle dish. Everything we ordered was medium spice, btw. Overall, I'm disappointed. I might give it another chance. And will update if I do.
